column1: # THE THREE DISTINCT BYTE-RANGE IDENTITIES, COMPUTED
# SEPARATELY.  They are different subjects and are NOT
# interchangeable, however similar the line numbers look.
This is the RECON07 frozen subject.  It is the frozen
# obligation, and it is what the C1 file CLAIMED to re-derive.
REPRODUCIBLE_AT=C0 and C1 with the exact RECON07 value
This is what the C1 file actually printed.  It is a COMMENT
# inside the helper block, not the decision.
SUBJECT=A COMMENT FRAGMENT ("* the AST graph, the allocation, the diagnostics, the recovery point or" / "* the token stream.")
SEMANTIC_IDENTITY=NOT A DECISION; NO BEHAVIOURAL MEANING
This is the actual post-refactor location of the SAME decision
# under the selector-OFF arm, with the single substitution
SUBJECT=THE MOVED LEGACY PREDICATE, selector-OFF #else arm (kind == AST_*)
## --- THE THREE IDENTITIES ARE MUTUALLY DISTINCT ---
# All three differ in digest AND in byte length AND in subject:
IDENTITY_1_EQUALS_IDENTITY_3=NO (the decision MOVED; the bytes changed by the stmt->kind -> kind substitution)
## --- THE TRUTHFUL RESTATEMENT OF THE C1 CLAIM ---
#   "The range is UNCHANGED at the entry commit"  and  "-> IDENTICAL".
#   The FROZEN RECON07 RANGE 1683..1684 HELD THE LEGACY INLINE
#   PREDICATE, digest a9fcb6a7..., 175 bytes, AT THE ENTRY
#   COMMIT, AT SLICE08 C0 AND AT SLICE08 C1.  That identity is
#   UNCHANGED.  The C1 file, however, PRINTED a9a33ff1...,
#   which is the digest of the SAME LINE NUMBERS in the POST-C2
#   tree, where they hold a COMMENT FRAGMENT.  The two digests
#   are not identical, and the C1 file did not reproduce its own
#   claimed command at the C1 commit.
ENTRY_RANGE_IDENTITY_UNCHANGED=YES (a9fcb6a7... at entry, C0 and C1)
